De Moivre's Theorem states that

$$
[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\phi )]^{n}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(n\phi )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(n\phi ).
$$

In our expression, we have $n=20$ and $\phi =\frac{2\theta }{5}.$ Substituting in these values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2\theta }{5})]}^{20} & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(20\cdot \frac{2\theta }{5})+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(20\cdot \frac{2\theta }{5}) \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\theta )+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$
